title: Docker Containers & Compose
description: Beginner-to-advanced Docker reference covering images, containers, Dockerfiles, BuildKit, cache, lifecycle, storage, networking, Compose, registries, multi-platform builds, security, diagnostics, and production practices.

sections.title: Images, Containers & Lifecycle
sections.description: Distinguish immutable image content from runtime process and writable state.

subtopics.title: Image, Container & Registry Mental Model
subtopics.description: An image is a content-addressed layer/config template; a container is an isolated process using that image plus runtime configuration and a writable layer; a registry distributes images.

diagram.content:
flowchart LR
  D[Dockerfile + context] --> B[BuildKit]
  B --> I[Immutable image layers]
  I --> R[Registry]
  I --> C1[Container process + writable layer]
  I --> C2[Container process + writable layer]
  V[Volume] --> C1

callouts.title: Containers Are Disposable
callouts.text: A container's writable layer disappears with removal. Persist application data in volumes or external services and design processes to restart safely.

subtopics.title: run, create, start, stop & remove
subtopics.description: run creates and starts; create separates configuration from start; stop sends the configured stop signal then kills after timeout; rm deletes stopped containers.

codeBlocks.code:
docker run --name web --detach --publish 8080:8080 --env-file .env app:1.4
docker ps --all
docker stop --time 30 web
docker start web
docker rm web

# Temporary interactive tool
docker run --rm -it --mount type=bind,src="$PWD",dst=/work -w /work alpine:3.22 sh

callouts.title: PID 1 Must Handle Signals
callouts.text: Use exec-form ENTRYPOINT/CMD so the application receives SIGTERM. Avoid shell wrappers that fail to exec or reap children; use --init when a tiny init is appropriate.

subtopics.title: inspect, exec, logs & stats
subtopics.description: Inspect declared/runtime state, execute short diagnostics in a running container, stream logs, and observe resource usage.

codeBlocks.code:
docker inspect web
docker logs --follow --tail 100 --timestamps web
docker exec -it web sh
docker top web
docker stats --no-stream web
docker port web
docker diff web

callouts.title: Do Not Repair Containers Manually
callouts.text: exec changes are unrepeatable and disappear after replacement. Diagnose, then fix the image/configuration and redeploy; never treat a running container like a hand-maintained VM.

sections.title: Dockerfiles & BuildKit
sections.description: Build reproducible minimal images with intentional cache and secret boundaries.

subtopics.title: FROM, WORKDIR, COPY, RUN, USER & CMD
subtopics.description: Each instruction contributes config or a filesystem layer. Use a pinned, maintained base; stable workdir; narrow COPY; non-root runtime; and one foreground process.

codeBlocks.code:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM node:24-alpine AS runtime
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY --chown=node:node package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci --omit=dev && npm cache clean --force
COPY --chown=node:node dist ./dist
USER node
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]

callouts.title: EXPOSE Is Documentation
callouts.text: It does not publish a host port. Use docker run -p or Compose ports; bind the application to 0.0.0.0 inside the container when it must accept external traffic.

subtopics.title: Layer Cache & .dockerignore
subtopics.description: Build cache reuses an instruction when its inputs match; once invalidated, following steps rebuild. Copy dependency manifests before frequently changing source.

tabs.label: Cache-Friendly
tabs.code:
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm npm ci
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

callouts.title: Context Is Data Sent to the Builder
callouts.text: Exclude secrets, VCS history, dependencies, and irrelevant artifacts. COPY . . can leak files into layers even if later deleted.

subtopics.title: Multi-Stage Builds, Secrets & Cache Mounts
subtopics.description: Build in a tool-rich stage and copy only runtime artifacts. BuildKit mounts provide temporary cache, secret, SSH, bind, or tmpfs data without committing it to layers.

codeBlocks.code:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
FROM node:24 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY package*.json ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.npm npm ci
COPY . .
RUN --mount=type=secret,id=npmrc,target=/root/.npmrc npm run build

FROM node:24-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /src/dist ./dist
USER node
CMD ["node", "dist/server.js"]

callouts.title: ARG and ENV Are Not Secret Storage
callouts.text: They can appear in metadata, history, cache, logs, or final config. Use secret mounts during build and runtime secret injection outside the image.

sections.title: Storage & Networking
sections.description: Choose explicit persistence, sharing, and connectivity contracts.

subtopics.title: Volumes, Bind Mounts & tmpfs
subtopics.description: Named volumes are Docker-managed persistent data; bind mounts expose host paths; tmpfs keeps temporary data in memory.

table.title: Container Storage Selection
rows: Must be backed up and lifecycle-managed separately
As long as host files exist
Source code, local config, host integration
Host coupling and accidental file exposure
Consumes memory and vanishes on stop
Poor choice for important or high-write data

codeBlocks.code:
docker volume create postgres-data
docker run --mount type=volume,src=postgres-data,dst=/var/lib/postgresql/data postgres:17
docker run --mount type=bind,src="$PWD/src",dst=/app/src,readonly app-dev
docker run --mount type=tmpfs,dst=/run/secrets,tmpfs-mode=0700 app

callouts.title: Mounts Override Image Paths
callouts.text: Mounting over a non-empty container directory hides image files. Define ownership/UID, backup/restore, migration, and removal policy for named volumes.

subtopics.title: Networks, DNS & Port Publishing
subtopics.description: User-defined bridge networks provide service-name DNS and isolation. Container ports are internal; published ports bind host interfaces.

codeBlocks.code:
docker network create app-net
docker run -d --name db --network app-net postgres:17
docker run -d --name api --network app-net -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 app
# API connects to db:5432, not localhost:5432.

callouts.title: localhost Means This Container
callouts.text: Use the other container's DNS/service name. Bind published development ports to 127.0.0.1 unless LAN exposure is intended.

subtopics.title: Resource Limits, Health & Restart
subtopics.description: Set memory/CPU/process limits, application-aware health checks, stop grace, and restart policy according to workload behavior.

codeBlocks.code:
docker run -d --name api \
  --memory 512m --cpus 1.0 --pids-limit 200 \
  --health-cmd='wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/health || exit 1' \
  --health-interval=30s --health-timeout=3s --health-retries=3 \
  --restart unless-stopped app:1.4

callouts.title: Restart Is Not Recovery
callouts.text: A crash loop can amplify dependency load and hide corruption. Emit diagnostics, use backoff/orchestration, make startup idempotent, and distinguish alive from ready.

sections.title: Docker Compose
sections.description: Define a trusted multi-container application with reproducible service, network, volume, and dependency configuration.

subtopics.title: Services, Networks, Volumes & Environment
subtopics.description: Compose services describe container configuration. Service names are network DNS names; named volumes persist; environment interpolation and container environment are distinct.

callouts.title: depends_on Is Not Application Resilience
callouts.text: Startup ordering/health can reduce races, but services must retry transient dependency loss after startup and shut down safely.

subtopics.title: Compose CLI, Profiles & Overrides
subtopics.description: Render effective configuration before applying; use profiles for optional tools and layered files carefully for environments.

codeBlocks.code:
docker compose config
docker compose up --detach --build --wait
docker compose ps
docker compose logs -f api
docker compose exec api sh
docker compose run --rm api npm test
docker compose --profile debug up
docker compose down
docker compose down --volumes  # deletes declared volumes

callouts.title: Compose Files Are Trusted Code
callouts.text: They can mount host files, request privileges, and expose secrets during interpolation/config rendering. Review remote Compose sources before running them.

subtopics.title: Development vs Production Compose
subtopics.description: Development may bind source and expose ports; production should use immutable tagged/digest-pinned images, controlled secrets, resource/policy settings, and external observability.

codeBlocks.code:
Development: build source, bind mounts, watch, debug ports, local dependencies
Production: pull verified image, no source bind, non-root/read-only, secrets, limits, health, logs
Use docker compose config with every file/env combination in CI.
Do not assume local Compose provides cluster scheduling, HA, rolling updates, or durable secret management.

callouts.title: Orchestration Boundary
callouts.text: See Kubernetes for reconciliation, replicas, rollout, Services, cluster scheduling, policy, and persistent-volume orchestration.

sections.title: Registries, Platforms & Supply Chain
sections.description: Publish immutable, verifiable artifacts for the target architecture.

subtopics.title: Tags, Digests, Login & Push
subtopics.description: Tags are mutable names; digests identify exact content. Authenticate with scoped tokens and promote tested digests rather than rebuilding per environment.

codeBlocks.code:
docker login registry.example.com
docker tag app:local registry.example.com/team/app:1.4.2
docker push registry.example.com/team/app:1.4.2
docker image inspect registry.example.com/team/app:1.4.2
docker pull registry.example.com/team/app@sha256:...

callouts.title: latest Is Not a Version
callouts.text: Deploy an immutable digest or unique release tag. Mutable tags make rollback, audit, cache, and incident diagnosis ambiguous.

subtopics.title: buildx & Multi-Platform Images
subtopics.description: Build a manifest list for target architectures using native builders, cross-compilation, or emulation; test runtime-native dependencies on each platform.

codeBlocks.code:
docker buildx create --use --name multi
docker buildx build \
  --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \
  --tag registry.example.com/team/app:1.4.2 \
  --provenance=true --sbom=true --push .

callouts.title: Emulation Can Hide Problems
callouts.text: QEMU builds may be slow and do not replace tests on target architecture. Pin platform-specific base images and verify native addons/binaries.

subtopics.title: SBOM, Provenance, Signing & Scanning
subtopics.description: Generate attestations during build, scan packages/config, sign or verify artifacts using your supply-chain system, and define vulnerability policy with ownership.

codeBlocks.code:
Build from pinned reviewed bases
Generate SBOM + provenance in CI
Scan OS and application dependencies
Sign/attest the pushed digest
Verify before deployment
Rebuild when base/security fixes arrive
Record exceptions with expiry and exploitability context

callouts.title: Scanning Is a Snapshot
callouts.text: New vulnerabilities appear after publication. Continuously rescan deployed digests and maintain a rebuild/patch cadence.

sections.title: Container Security & Hardening
sections.description: Minimize privileges, writable surface, secrets, attack tools, and daemon trust.

subtopics.title: Non-Root, Capabilities & Read-Only Filesystem
subtopics.description: Set a numeric non-root user, drop capabilities, avoid privileged mode/host namespaces/socket mounts, and make root filesystem read-only with explicit writable mounts.

callouts.title: Docker Socket Equals Host Control
callouts.text: Mounting /var/run/docker.sock generally grants control equivalent to root on the host. Use purpose-built restricted APIs/builders instead.

subtopics.title: Minimal Images & Runtime Secrets
subtopics.description: Ship only runtime files and libraries, omit shells/package managers when feasible, and mount/inject secrets at runtime with rotation and access controls.

codeBlocks.code:
Do not COPY .env, credentials, SSH keys, cloud config, or VCS history
Do not pass secrets via image ARG/ENV or command-line where metadata exposes them
Prefer runtime secret files/agents over broad environment where supported
Never log effective config containing secrets
Separate build credentials from runtime credentials

callouts.title: Smaller Is Not Automatically Safer
callouts.text: Minimal images reduce surface but still need provenance, updates, compatible libraries, and usable diagnostics. Choose maintained bases and test operational needs.

subtopics.title: Daemon, Desktop & Host Boundary
subtopics.description: Anyone controlling the Docker daemon can usually control the host. Protect its API, groups, contexts, credentials, and build agents.

codeBlocks.code:
Never expose unauthenticated Docker TCP API
Treat membership in docker group as privileged
Use TLS/SSH contexts for remote engines
Separate untrusted builds and apply quotas
Review bind mounts, device access, host network/PID, privileged, capabilities
Keep Engine/Desktop/host kernel patched

callouts.title: Container Isolation Is Not a VM Guarantee
callouts.text: Containers share the host kernel. Use stronger sandbox/VM isolation for hostile multi-tenancy and enforce kernel, runtime, and orchestration security controls.

sections.title: Diagnostics, Cleanup & Checklist
sections.description: Debug layer-by-layer and remove only resolved, explicitly targeted resources.

subtopics.title: Build & Runtime Troubleshooting
subtopics.description: Inspect effective build stages, history, image config, mounts, networks, DNS, logs, health, and process signals.

codeBlocks.code:
docker build --progress=plain --target build .
docker history --no-trunc app:1.4.2
docker inspect app:1.4.2
docker inspect web --format '{{json .State.Health}}'
docker network inspect app-net
docker volume inspect db-data
docker events --since 10m

callouts.title: Debug Without Changing the Artifact
callouts.text: Use an ephemeral debug image/container joined to the same network/volumes when the production image intentionally lacks a shell.

subtopics.title: Disk Usage & Safe Cleanup
subtopics.description: Measure images, layers, containers, volumes, and build cache before pruning; unused volumes may contain the only copy of data.

codeBlocks.code:
docker system df --verbose
docker ps -a --filter status=exited
docker image ls --digests
docker volume ls
docker builder prune --filter until=168h
docker image prune
# Review targets before any system/volume prune.

callouts.title: Volume Deletion Is Data Deletion
callouts.text: Confirm ownership, backup, and restore before docker volume rm, compose down -v, or volume prune. Prune commands are not routine harmless cleanup.

subtopics.title: Production Checklist
subtopics.description: Review reproducibility, runtime ownership, persistence, exposure, supply chain, privilege, and operations.

codeBlocks.code:
□ Base and deployed images are pinned/traceable by digest
□ Multi-stage image contains only runtime artifacts
□ .dockerignore excludes secrets and irrelevant context
□ Build secrets use mounts, never ARG/ENV/layers
□ Process runs non-root and handles SIGTERM as PID 1
□ Writable data uses explicit volumes/external stores
□ Ports bind only intended interfaces
□ CPU, memory, PIDs, health, and stop grace are defined
□ Root filesystem/capabilities/privileges are minimized
□ Logs go to stdout/stderr without secrets
□ Image is scanned, attested, patched, and multi-platform tested
□ Compose effective config is reviewed and dependencies retry
□ Backup/restore and safe rollback are proven
□ Debug and cleanup procedures avoid mutating/deleting data
